course_title: Project Management for Tourism and Events
course_description:
This course integrates project management theory with practice and equips students with the knowledge and skills to plan and deliver a diverse range of projects in the tourism and events sectors. The course requires students to demonstrate critical judgement and creativity in the application of design, project management, and technological innovations in the execution of successful projects.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

The course was previously delivered in a blended learning format, comprising a 1-hour online lecture and a 2-hour tutorial each week. In response to student feedback requesting increased contact time, the course has been redesigned as a weekly 3-hour interactive seminar.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills to successfully plan and stage different types of projects, including operations, logistics and primarily events. In the context of events, the courseﾠexplores a variety of operational issues which are significant for effective event management such as creativity and design, risk and emergency management, and managing staff/volunteers.

learning_outcomes.description: Discuss the theoretical and practical components of project planning and operations
Use international case studies to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of event design principles
Develop operational plans to strategically facilitate effective and efficient planning and management of events and tourism-related projects
Critically engage with issues of risk management, workforce, and logistics
Work effectively in teams to identify and propose solutions for real-world tourism and events operational issues

assessment_details.task_description: Three non-cumulative review quizzes (10% each) will be administered throughout the semester that will cover the course lecture material, readings, and the tutorial activities. 60 minutes will be allowed to complete each quiz between 8am and 8pm on the scheduled date. Each quiz will consist of 10 questions consisting of an array of question types. The questions will primarily require you to individually complete the problem based learning activities from our weekly seminars. Question types will include open response, submission of files, drawing figures, constructing charts, multiple choice, true/false and/or short answer questions drawn from the class content from the preceding weeks of content. All quizzes will be completed fully online via Inspera Assessment. Inspera Assessment provides additional functionality to complement the existing suite of digital learning tools at UQ with a greater range of question types, accessibility provisions, and non-English languages. A formative practice quiz to allow students to gain familiarity with the types of questions to be asked will be available from the start of the course. assessment_details.title: Client Event Tourism Proposal
assessment_details.due_date: Exam week 1 - Exam week 2 Presentations will be scheduled during exam period. Date to be released during the term as scheduled by the the UQ Examinations Office.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Peer assessment factor, Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Students will work in teams of four to six throughout the semester to develop an Event Tourism Proposal for a real client from the Brisbane business community. In Week 4, the client will present a series of event tourism briefs directly to the class. Each team will select or be allocated a brief and develop a proposal addressing the client’s real-world problems and objectives. The proposal will incorporate key topics covered in the course, including: Overview, purpose, concept, market, feasibility, timing site selection and layout; staffing and volunteer requirements; staging and logistics; risk management; and financing and budgeting. Teams must apply the project management tools developed throughout the semester, including Gantt charts, run sheets, work breakdown structures and site maps. The project will be completed in partnership with EventsAir, an industry-leading event management software platform. Students will receive training in EventsAir and use the platform to support the development of their proposals. Teams will be formed by students, with assistance from the teaching staff, in Week 1. Students will remain in these teams throughout the semester. At the end of the semester, each team will deliver its proposal directly to the client and teaching staff through: a pitch of no more than 10 minutes; a five-minute oral defence conducted through a question-and-answer session; and a written proposal of no more than 15 single-sided pages. All team members must contribute to the pitch and respond to questions during the oral defence. Marks will reflect each student’s individual contribution to the assessment task. Students must complete confidential peer evaluations at both the middle and end of the semester. Individual grades will be calculated by weighting the team’s overall assessment score according to each student’s peer-evaluation score, including their self-evaluation. Complete assessment instructions and marking criteria will be provided on Blackboard. Students are encouraged to consult the following group-work resources: UQ Study Skills: Group Work Working in Teams: A Practical Guide Please note that the presentation and oral defence will be recorded for marking purposes in accordance with UQ policy.
